stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab may approach Odisha coast; Kerala puts 10 districts under orange alert
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab may approach Odisha coast; Kerala puts 10 districts under orange alert
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The IMD has warned that Cyclone Arnab could develop over the Bay of Bengal by October 26, with winds gusting up to 90 kmph and a possible approach towards the Andhra Pradesh–Odisha coast.
Meanwhile, 10 Kerala districts are under an orange alert for heavy rain on October 24.

New Delhi: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned that a cyclonic storm could develop over the Bay of Bengal by October 26 and move towards the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast around October 28.
Meanwhile, Kerala is expected to experience continued heavy rainfall, with orange alerts issued in 10 districts on Saturday, October 24.
The IMD has forecast the development of a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26.

The weather system, which was identified as a low-pressure area over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday, October 23, is expected to intensify into a depression on October 24 before strengthening further.

According to the forecast, the system could develop into a cyclonic storm by October 26 and move west-northwestwards towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts over the following two days.
If the system develops into a cyclone, it will be named Arnab, a name proposed by Bangladesh.
IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said wind speeds could reach 70–80 kmph, with gusts of up to 90 kmph, from the morning of October 26.
Wind speeds and the storm's intensity could increase as the system develops.
The exact path and landfall location have not yet been confirmed.
Odisha authorities said greater clarity on the system's movement could emerge by Saturday.

stories.headline: Cabinet Sub-Committee seeks to draw up department-wise plan to tackle El Nino induced drought conditions
stories.title: Cabinet Sub-Committee seeks to draw up department-wise plan to tackle El Nino induced drought conditions
stories.summary: 358 mandals provisionally identified as drought-affected based on rainfall, crop coverage
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Cabinet Sub-Committee on Drought and El Nino conditions chaired by Deputy Chief Minister M. Bhatti Vikramarka on Friday resolved to prepare a comprehensive and department-wise action plan to tackle the drought caused by El Nino conditions.

The plans will focus on safeguarding supply of water for drinking and irrigation and ensuring uninterrupted electricity, agricultural support and rural employment so that people do not face hardships in the coming days.

The first meeting of the Cabinet Sub-Committee, constituted to review the drought and El Nino situation in the State and recommend appropriate measures to the government, was held here on Friday (October 23).
The meeting primarily discussed the impact of El Nino and drought in various parts of the State, water availability, relief measures for farmers and future action plans.

Sub-Committee members and Ministers N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy, D. Seethakka, Tummala Nageswara Rao and Vakiti Srihari along with Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju and secretaries of the concerned departments attended the meeting.
Mr. Vikramarka asked the officials to scientifically assess drought conditions and examine the mandals eligible for declaration as drought-affected areas under the prescribed guidelines.
He stressed that the government’s priority was to minimise the impact of drought and ensure timely delivery of necessary assistance to people through coordinated efforts.
He instructed officials to assess not only areas already experiencing severe drought but also mandals where the drought impact exceeds 20%.
An advance assessment of the likely impact of drought on various sectors would help the government provide timely assistance to those in need, he said.
He suggested that every department identify the challenges and prepare a clear action plan to address them.
He asked the officials to anticipate challenges in the power sector arising from El Nino conditions and take measures in advance.
Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy asked the District Collectors to conduct weekly review meetings with the officials concerned to monitor the measures being implemented to address the drought conditions.

stories.headline: India U-19 Women’s Teams to Face Nepal in Bengaluru Tri-Series Ahead of World Cup
stories.title: India U-19 Women’s Teams to Face Nepal in Bengaluru Tri-Series Ahead of World Cup
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in title weight 42
article_sentences: New Delhi: Two India U-19 women’s sides will take on Nepal in a tri-series at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru from November 10 to 22, as the two-time defending champions look to enter the final leg of preparations ahead of next year’s U19 World Cup.

According to a press release issued by Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) secretary Paras Khadka, the series will feature India U-19 Women’s ‘A’ and India U-19 Women’s ‘B’ alongside Nepal’s U-19 women’s team.
India U-19 ‘B’ team will first take on Nepal on November 12, before the visitors face India ‘A’ side on November 14.
India U-19 ‘B’ team will take on Nepal in the first reverse fixture of November 18, before India U-19 ‘A’ take on the visitors on November 20.
The tri-series will conclude with the final on November 22, with all matches having 1pm start time.

stories.headline: Delhi court orders trial against Yasin Malik, six others in money laundering case
stories.title: Delhi court orders trial against Yasin Malik, six others in money laundering case
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 24: A special NIA court in New Delhi has ordered a trial against Yasin Malik, Zahoor Ahmed Shah Watali, Abdul Rashid Sheikh, Shabir Ahmad Shah, Naval Kishore Kapoor, Trison Farms and Construction Pvt Ltd, and Masarat Alam Bhat in Rs 8.9 crore money laundering case, according to a report in The News Mill. According to the report, the accused received the said amount through hawala channels from the Pakistani establishment. The charges stem from a case initially registered by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in 2017. The accused are charged under Sections 120B, 121, and 121A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), as well as Sections 13, 16, 17, 18, 20, 38, 39, and 40 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma, as per the report, ordered the trial to begin, with prosecution evidence recording scheduled to start on November 19. The hearing was conducted in a closed courtroom. Malik appeared via video conferencing from Tihar Jail and denied the charges, stating he will contest the case. In September, the court had framed charges against Malik and six others under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). It is alleged that the accused received funds from the Pakistani establishment and other terrorist organisations to support secessionist activities in Jammu and Kashmir. The court found sufficient prima facie evidence to charge all seven accused under Section 3 of the PMLA, punishable under Section 4.
